problem: GitHub Actions accumulated 19 in_progress runs and 121 queued runs while repository delivery recovery continued creating recovery work.
root_cause: Powerhouse Delivery Recovery Supervisor was triggered both on every push to main and every five minutes. With 55 open pull requests, one repository-wide scan could dispatch Required test and Unified Brain Delivery recovery work for multiple PRs. Recovery traffic therefore amplified control-plane saturation instead of applying backpressure.
prevention: Repository-wide delivery recovery must never run on every main push.
Recovery scanning is scheduled/manual only and uses a lower cadence.
Open a repository-wide circuit breaker when active or queued Actions work reaches the configured threshold.
Allow at most one PR recovery per supervisor cycle.
Suppress duplicate recovery dispatch when an equivalent active run already exists.
CI must regression-test these backpressure invariants so later workflow changes cannot silently restore fan-out.
Website release-risk must classify recovery-supervisor workflow and its regression tests as non-artifact control-plane changes, so CI-only fixes never launch full public-site browser crawls.
Queued runs older than six hours are eligible for janitor cancellation only when their non-main head branch no longer exists.
Stale queue cleanup is bounded to twenty cancellations per supervisor cycle and runs before the active-run circuit breaker is evaluated.
Every material GitHub mutation must forecast queue pressure and projected fan-out before execution.
Soft pressure begins at 12 active or 10 queued runs; hard circuit opens at 20 active or 20 queued runs.
A single action may not intentionally create more than six new runs; batch or narrow before mutation.
One obligation has one executable PR and one active Required/BRAIN instance per PR/head.
Borging, documentation, learning and skill changes for one obligation should be committed atomically when safe.
Agents and chats must treat predicted queue amplification as a pre-mutation blocker, not something to clean up afterward.
Governance, agent policy, skill and delivery-controller changes are non-artifact control-plane and must not trigger website preview/browser lanes unless a real website artifact also changes.
The website browser lane has a hard 15-minute timeout so a browser stall cannot retain runner capacity indefinitely.
Stale in-progress Actions runs are cancelled only after 1800 seconds without progress and only when their delivery identity is obsolete.
A queued or in-progress run is obsolete when its PR is closed, its PR/branch head moved away from the run SHA, its non-main branch disappeared, or its main SHA is no longer current.
Branch existence alone is never proof that an old queued run is still authoritative.
Unexpected candidate-head movement must be diff-validated against the previously trusted head before the new head can inherit delivery authority.
Workflow YAML repairs must preserve existing structural regression anchors when semantics do not require changing them.

Before inserting a job-level control such as timeout-minutes, run or inspect the tests that assert neighboring YAML key order; prefer a placement that preserves both semantics and established contract.
Proven obsolete GitHub Actions runs use bounded escalation: normal cancel, then force-cancel, then delete fallback only when identity is already proven obsolete.
A recovery budget loop must use process substitution or another non-piped iterator so breaking after the budget cannot SIGPIPE jq and falsely fail the supervisor.
Terminal closure must allow normal protected Required duration; the bounded exact-head gate wait is fifteen minutes inside a thirty-minute job timeout.
Historical one-off Outcome Obligation Sweep failures are not current-main failures when later same-main sweeps succeed; use latest-current-main evidence.

Provider-control-plane zombies are runs whose delivery identity is obsolete but GitHub rejects normal cancel, force-cancel and delete; record them explicitly and subtract them from effective admission pressure while retaining raw telemetry.
Recovery supervisor cadence is five minutes, proven obsolete queued identity can be reaped after 60 seconds and proven obsolete in-progress identity after 300 seconds.
Queue governor defaults are soft 8 total active / 5 queued and hard 12 total active / 8 queued, with projected fan-out capped at 3.

evidence.website_timeout_structural_contract: browser job keeps needs immediately after job label; timeout follows needs

failed_approaches: Repository-wide recovery on every main push plus a five-minute schedule.
Dispatching recovery independently across many open PRs during runner saturation.
Treating each borging/documentation/learning edit as a separate CI-triggering commit.
Creating successor recovery PRs before eliminating duplicate-obligation conflicts.
Following superseded workflow runs after the PR head had moved.
Allowing control-plane-only fixes to trigger full website/browser/artifact verification.
Letting queued runs survive after their PR was merged and their branch no longer existed.
Refreshing a PR through transient branch equality with main, which can auto-close the PR.
Carrying unrelated baseline failures inside queue repair instead of fixing the canonical baseline first.
Leaving the website browser lane without an explicit timeout, allowing a non-artifact governance PR to occupy a runner indefinitely.
Failing to classify AGENTS.md, brain/policies, .agents/skills and tools/delivery as non-artifact control-plane paths.
Treating branch existence as sufficient evidence that a queued run was still live; PR #1444 remained merged while its branch later pointed at a different SHA.
Allowing stale in-progress runs from superseded PR heads and old main epochs to retain runner slots indefinitely.
Silently accepting an unexpected candidate head without first validating the exact diff from the previously trusted head.
Inserting timeout-minutes between the browser job label and its required needs anchor; YAML remained valid but broke the established composable-release structural regression.
Using only the normal workflow cancel endpoint for corrupted historical queued runs; GitHub kept the runs queued and both janitors failed every schedule.
Piping jq into a while loop and breaking when the one-PR recovery budget was consumed; jq received SIGPIPE and the supervisor ended red despite respecting its budget.
Allowing only five minutes for terminal closure to observe Required; normal long Required runs caused false terminal failures after the PR had already merged.
Counting proven uncancellable GitHub control-plane zombies as authoritative delivery pressure forever, which can deadlock admission even when those records have zero executable jobs.
